title: Electricity: Circuits and their Components
seo_title: Electricity Class 7 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3)
standard_text: Electric cell and battery, bulb and its filament, switch, closed and open circuits; circuit diagrams with symbols; conductors and insulators; safety with electricity; LEDs (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 7 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 3: cells, batteries, bulbs, switches, open and closed circuits, circuit symbols, conductors and insulators and electrical safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Current flows only in a closed circuit.
key_sub: Conductors let current pass; insulators do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

An electric cell has a positive and a negative terminal. When a cell, wires, a switch and a bulb make a complete path, the circuit is closed and current flows, so the bulb's filament glows. If there is a gap (an open switch or a broken filament), the circuit is open and no current flows.

Metals such as copper, iron and aluminium, and graphite, are conductors; rubber, plastic, wood and glass are insulators. Two cells joined positive to negative make a battery and a brighter bulb. Never touch switches with wet hands or play with the mains supply.

Example

Switch OFF: does the bulb glow?

the circuit is open

Answer: no

Example

A rubber eraser in the gap?

rubber is an insulator

Answer: the bulb does not glow

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bulb glows when the circuit has a gap.
  • Calling graphite an insulator.
  • Joining cells positive to positive.
